Credit costs are the expense of maintaining funding sources for the unused credit line of each account. Credit costs are based on two profit parameter values: the loan equivalence factor and the line of credit rate. There are two steps in calculating credit costs: 1. The unused line of each account is multiplied by a “loan equivalence factor”  - this factor represents the probability of the customer drawing down the unused line. The resulting dollar value is referred to as the “loan equivalent” of the unused line. 2. The unused line’s loan equivalent is multiplied by a line of credit rate

Equity credit for each account is calculated by multiplying the equity credit rate by the equity allocated to the account. Equity is allocated to each account based on the account’s average daily balance and equity allocation factor. The equity can be used to partially fund the balance of each account – this equity credit can therefore be thought of as an offset to the cost of funds. The dollar amount of equity credit assigned to each account is calculated for each month of the quarter as follows: Equity Credit ($ = [(Average daily balance * (Equity Allocation Factor * (Equity Credit Rate]/12 where the value for the equity credit rate is supplied by issuer.
